en: The Garuḍa Upaniṣad
That which exceeds Brahman is poison; that which is Brahman alone is nectar.
That which exceeds Brahman is like poison; that which is Brahman alone, O sky-farer, is my day.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods.
O worshipful ones, may we behold what is auspicious with our eyes.
With steady limbs and bodies, they offered praise.
May we attain that lifespan ordained by the gods.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being.
May Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel is unbroken, grant us well-being.
May Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
Hari Om! I shall proclaim the Garuḍa-Brahmavidyā, that knowledge which Brahmā taught to Nārada, Nārada to Bṛhatsena, Bṛhatsena to Indra,
Indra to Bharadvāja, and Bharadvāja imparted to his disciples who desired long life.
Of this Śrī Mahāgaruḍa Brahmavidyā, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi),
Gāyatrī is the meter (chanda),
and the Blessed Lord Mahāgaruḍa is the deity (devatā).
The application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of pleasing the illustrious Mahāgaruḍa and for the destruction of all my poisons during the recitation:
*Oṃ namo bhagavate* to the two thumbs.
To Śrī Mahāgaruḍa, svāhā with the two index fingers; to Pakṣīndra, vaṣaṭ with the two middle fingers;
to Śrī Viṣṇuvallabha, huṃ with the two ring fingers.
*Vauṣaṭ* with both little fingers to the one worshipped by the three worlds;
*phaṭ* with the palms and backs of the hands to the one whose form is like a fierce and terrifying fire of time (*kālānala*).
Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the heart and other limbs.
The binding of the directions (*digbandha*) is performed with the mantra *bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar oṃ*. The visualization (*dhyāna*):
the right foot is in the *svastika* posture, while the left foot is drawn up.
Garuḍa, the beloved of Hari, with his two arms joined in the añjali gesture.
Ananta is the bracelet on the left arm, while Vāsuki is the sacred thread;
Takṣaka is the waist-band, and Kārkoṭa is said to be the necklace.
Padma is on the right ear, while Mahāpadma is on the left;
Śaṅkha is in the region of the head, and Gulika is between the arms.
It was conquered by the two yakṣas Pauṇḍraka and Ālikanāga, and was joyfully served by Elāputraka, Nāga, and others. (4)
He had tawny eyes, was Garuḍa, possessed a radiance like gold,
long arms, broad shoulders, and was adorned with ornaments of sound.
From the navel upward it was golden-hued, from the navel to the hips it had the brilliance of snow,
from the hips to the neck it was red as saffron, and its face resembled a hundred moons.
His face had a blue-tipped nose and large, beautiful earrings;
his mouth was formidable with protruding fangs, and he was radiant with a crown and diadem.
O vehicle of Viṣṇu, whose every limb is reddened with saffron and whose face is as white as the kunda flower and the moon—salutations to you; grant me constant well-being. (8)
Thus one should meditate upon Garuḍa, adorned with serpents, during the three junctions of the day;
he quickly destroys poison, just as fire consumes a tuft of cotton.
Oṃ oṃ oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the glorious Mahāgaruḍa, lord of birds, beloved of Viṣṇu, worshipped by the three worlds, whose form is like the fierce and terrifying fire of time,
with adamantine claws, an adamantine beak, adamantine teeth, and adamantine fangs.
O you whose body is marked by a vajra-tail and vajra-wings, *om īhī ehi*, O Śrī Mahāgaruḍa, enter, enter this command;
corrupt, corrupt the poison of the wicked; destroy, destroy those who have been touched!

Tear asunder, tear asunder the poison of the biting serpents! Destroy, destroy the latent poison! Annihilate, annihilate all poison! Slay, slay! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Reduce to ashes, reduce to ashes! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
O you who resemble the lunar disc, who hold the solar disc in your fist, whose limbs bear the seal of the terrestrial mandala—to the illustrious Mahāgaruḍa, remove, remove the poison! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Oṃ kṣipa svāhā.

Oṃ īṃ! She moves, she moves; she acts as such, she acts for me. She who is the form of poison among poisons, the corrupter of poison, the dryer of poison, the destroyer of poison, the remover of poison—poison is slain, poison is destroyed, poison is dissolved within, poison is utterly annihilated.
The poison is destroyed by Brahmā; the poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt, svāhā!

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Great Garuḍa, the vehicle of Viṣṇu, worshipped by the three worlds, possessing adamantine claws and an adamantine beak, whose body is adorned with adamantine wings! Come, come, O Great Garuḍa! Cut, cut the poison!
Possess, possess [it]! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; the Trivṛt is your head, the Gāyatra is your eye, the Stoma is your body,

the Vāmadevya Sāman is your torso, the Bṛhat and Rathantara are your wings, the Yajñāyajñīya is your tail, the meters are your limbs, the Dhiṣṇiya hearths are your hooves, and the Yajus formulas are your name.

You are the fair-winged Garuḍa; go to heaven, fly to the light! Om! This Brahma-vidyā was spoken of old on the new moon and the full moon. It moves, it moves with him who practices it; it is my practice. It is the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison, the remover of poison.
Poison is slain, poison is destroyed, poison is utterly destroyed; it is slain by the thunderbolt of Indra. Svāhā!

To her: "Whether you are the messenger of Anantaka, or whether Anantaka himself moves about, [this mantra] moves accordingly; it acts upon me, it destroys poison, it neutralizes poison—poison is slain, poison is destroyed."
The poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt; the poison is destroyed by your *brahman*-power; the poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt—*svāhā*!
Whether you are the messenger of Vāsuki, or whether Vāsuki himself moves about, he moves about.
She who acts for that, she who acts for me, the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison—poison is slain, poison is destroyed!
Poison is slain by the thunderbolt of Indra; poison is slain by your *brahman*-power;
poison is slain by the thunderbolt of Indra, *svāhā*! Whether it be Takṣaka himself who moves about.

Sacarati, tatkārī, matkārī, viṣanāśinī, viṣadūṣiṇī; the poison is struck down, the poison is destroyed; the poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra, the poison is struck down by Brahmā, the poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra, svāhā!

If you are the messenger of Karkoṭaka, or if Karkoṭaka himself is moving about—moving about indeed!—[I am] she who acts against him, acting against me, the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison. Poison is slain, poison is destroyed;
poison is slain by the thunderbolt of Indra. Poison is slain by Brahmā for you; poison [is slain] by the thunderbolt of Indra. Svāhā!

If you are the messenger of Padmaka, or if you are Padmaka himself, move! Move! You who act accordingly, you who act for me, the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison—poison is struck down, poison is destroyed!
Poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra; poison is struck down by Brahmā for you.
The poison [is struck] by Indra's thunderbolt; svāhā!

If you are the messenger of Mahāpadmaka, or if you are Mahāpadmaka himself, moving about or acting as his agent—[I invoke] the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison: the poison is slain, the poison is destroyed! The poison is struck down by Indra’s thunderbolt; the poison is struck down by Brahmā for you.
The poison [is struck] by Indra’s thunderbolt; svāhā!

If you are the messenger of Śaṅkhaka, or if Śaṅkhaka himself is moving about—moving about indeed!—then may she who acts as such act for me; may she be the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison!
Poison is slain, poison is destroyed; the poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra.
Your poison has been destroyed by the Brahmā; by Indra’s thunderbolt, svāhā!

Whether you are Gulikadūta or Gulika himself, move! Move! You who act accordingly, you who act for me, the destroyer of poison, the defiler of poison, the remover of poison—poison is slain, poison is destroyed; the poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra.
Your poison has been destroyed by the Brahma-weapon; [destroyed] by Indra’s thunderbolt, svāhā!

Whether you are the messenger of Pauṇḍraka Ālika, or whether Pauṇḍraka Ālika himself moves about, he who acts thus acts against me. [I am] the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison, the remover of poison;
the poison is slain, the poison is destroyed, the poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra.
The poison is destroyed by the Brahman; the poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt, svāhā!

If you are a messenger of the Nāgas, or if you are a Nāga yourself, move about! Move about! You who act accordingly, you who act for me, the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison, the remover of poison—the poison is slain, the poison is destroyed! The poison is struck down by the thunderbolt of Indra; your poison is struck down!
By Brahmā, the poison of Indra with the thunderbolt; svāhā!
Whether it be from spiders, secondary spiders, scorpions, or centipedes,

or from any moving or stationary creature— if it moves upon one, this [mantra] is its counteractant, my counteractant, the destroyer of poison, the corrupter of poison, and the remover of poison; the poison is struck down, the poison is destroyed.
The poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt; the poison is destroyed by your sacred spell (*brahman*); the poison is destroyed by Indra’s thunderbolt, *svāhā*!
Of these divine ones—Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Padmaka, Mahāpadmaka, Śaṅkhaka, Gulika, Pauṇḍraka, Ālika, and Nāgaka—[the poison is destroyed].

Of great serpents, those with the forms of great serpents, those with poisonous mouths, those with poisonous teeth, those with poisonous fangs, those with poisonous limbs, those with poisonous tails, those that roam everywhere, scorpions, spiders, *pralūtās*, mice, and house-lizards.
Of house-lizards, snakes, and those born from the dark fire-pits and anthills of house-mountain-caverns;

of those born of grass, leaves, and wood, dwelling in the hollows of trees and timber; of those produced from roots, bark, wood, resin, leaves, flowers, and fruits; and of wicked insects, monkeys, dogs, cats, jackals, tigers, and boars—whether viviparous, oviparous, soil-born, or sweat-born.
[It protects] from those caused by weapons, arrows, cuts, eruptions, wounds, and great sores; from artificial [poisons];
and from others that cause fear—such as spirits (bhūta), vetālas, kūṣmāṇḍas, piśācas, pretas, rākṣasas, and yakṣas—as well as from those with poisonous mouths, fangs, limbs, tails, or horns.
She who has the form of poison, she who corrupts poison, she who dries up poison, she who destroys poison, she who removes poison—
poison is slain, poison is destroyed; the poison is dissolved within, the poison is utterly lost, the poison is slain by Brahmā with the thunderbolt of Indra, svāhā!
Whoever should read or hear this knowledge of Brahman on the new moon day, for as long as they live, serpents shall not harm them.
Having caused eight Brahmins to master it, one may be liberated even by a blade of grass.
Having caused a hundred Brahmins to grasp it, one should release it with the eye;
having caused a thousand Brahmins to grasp it, one should release it with the mind. Serpents do not release [their venom] into water.
"They do not release it in grass; they do not release it in wood," so said the Blessed One. "Brahman is the Upaniṣad."
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods.
O worshipful ones, may we behold what is auspicious with our eyes.
Praising with steadfast limbs and bodies.
May we attain the lifespan ordained by the gods.
May Indra of far-reaching fame grant us well-being.
May Pūṣan, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel is unimpaired, grant us well-being.
May Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.
Hariḥ Oṃ Tat Sat.
Thus ends the Śrī Gāruḍa Upaniṣad.
